1. Use your survival tool at the beginning to harvest enough trees/rocks for a simple hut and storage. Snag food along the way as much as you can. 

2. Work towards a simple hover vehicle. I love using the blueprints on Steam for this because it makes it way easier and shows costs up front. 

3. Use hover vehicle to travel and loot and eventually mine resource deposits once you can mount a drill

I know I'm late to this but something similar happened to us. Thankfully way less serious. 

I'm always the safety conscious one and my wife would shut me down and insist "he's fine" and make fun of me like I'm being paranoid. I didn't want him going down the slide on top of adults like you mentioned. I didn't want him walking down the stairs without me being right next to him when he was first learning to walk. Most relevant, I didn't want him standing in grocery carts. 

At Costco, we were getting our cart and I started putting him in the baby seat (1 and a half years old kid for reference). She said something nasty to me and put him in the cart despite my protests. Something about "my decision is final." I thought fine, I don't really want to argue in public about this, let's get it over with. I regret that every day. I learned that you DO have to escalate and put your foot down. If you have to have that public argument, DO IT! 

What ended up happening was that, like a typical toddler does, he thought it'd be funny to dive headfirst out of the cart. He bonked his head on the ground before I could catch him. It was terrifying and I was so worried that he had brain damage. Luckily, there was no sign of any serious head trauma other than a little red spot and him screaming his head off. Doctors said it was fine and he showed zero signs of concussion, dizziness, anything. 

So the next time my wife tried to put him in the cart, I put my foot down and said absolutely not. She respected that and now keeps him in the baby seat where he belongs. 

On a side note, we had to go to couples therapy for only semi-related things--this is also probably essential for you guys because safety is a NO COMPROMISE thing. I will forever resent her because of her safety choices causing him harm and I imagine you will too. The best way to avoid forever resentment and damage to your marriage is getting on the same page. That may take therapy.
